structuralDecisions.decision: Resolve the open cross-file isolation question: protect every read/write of apps/mock-api/data/expeditions.json with one exclusive mutex, shared by reagent-map-save.spec.ts, reagent-map-api.spec.ts, and reagent-map-expeditions.spec.ts. Implement acquire/release as plain exported functions inside reagent-map-api.spec.ts (it already owns the seed-capture/restore pattern) and import them into the other two files. Lock acquisition polls with Playwright's own expect(fn).toPass({ timeout: 30_000 }) around an atomic fs.openSync(lockPath, 'wx') — EEXIST means someone else holds it, toPass's built-in retry/backoff handles the wait. Release is fs.unlinkSync. The lock file itself lives at path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'reagent-map-expeditions.lock'), never under a tracked path, so it can never be an out-of-scope file change (it is created and deleted at runtime, never committed). Each of the three files keeps/adds test.describe.configure({ mode: 'serial' }) and acquires the lock in beforeAll (after capturing seed) and releases it in afterAll, restoring seed content in afterEach exactly as reagent-map-api.spec.ts already does — this guarantees no worker's test body (where the live GET/POST against the one shared mock-api process actually happens) can interleave with another file's mutation, while each file's own internal tests stay serial as today.
structuralDecisions.rationale: playwright.config.ts (fullyParallel: true, one shared webServer, no project dependencies) is outside scope.paths, so the mechanism cannot live in config — it must live inside files matching tests/reagent-map-*.spec.ts, which rules out a separate non-spec helper module too (also out of scope). All three specs hit the same running mock-api instance (one webServer, reused across workers), so the race is real: reagent-map-expeditions.spec.ts's exact-count assertions run against a live GET that happens inside the test body, not at its static top-of-file JSON import (that import only supplies the three seeded expeditions' fixed names/ids, which no test ever mutates), so lock coverage starting in beforeAll is sufficient — the static import races nothing. A single exclusive lock (not separate read/write locks) is correct here because writes are infrequent relative to the whole suite and the simplicity of one mutex avoids a reader/writer protocol this test suite doesn't need.
tradeOffs: A stale lock (worker crash mid-test while holding it) hangs every subsequent run against the same temp path until the stale lock file is manually deleted — mitigated by a before-retry staleness check (see fitness/judgmentOnly entry below) but not eliminated.

Serializing all expeditions.json-touching specs across files reduces the effective parallelism --workers=3 is meant to buy for this subset of the suite — acceptable because the claim's own Test Approach already says to run the full suite one image at a time and treat these specs as a small, known-serial slice.

Duplicated-looking beforeAll/afterEach/afterAll scaffolding appears in three files instead of one; the alternative (a shared non-spec helper module) is blocked by scope.paths, so this is the in-scope trade, not a design preference.

structuralDecisions.decision: The lock's retry loop is built entirely from Playwright's own expect(fn).toPass({ timeout }) polling primitive, never a hand-rolled for/while plus sleep.
structuralDecisions.rationale: architecture-guardrails.md #5 bans custom retry-with-sleep loops and requires a framework-provided CircuitBreaker or ExponentialBackoffStrategy. toPass() is @playwright/test's own built-in polling-with-backoff mechanism for exactly this kind of 'retry until a side-effecting check stops throwing' case — using it instead of a hand-written while(true){...; await sleep(...)} satisfies the guardrail's intent in test tooling, the same way the guardrail is satisfied in production code by a named resilience strategy class.
tradeOffs: toPass()'s default interval schedule is a fixed Playwright default, not independently tuned for this lock — acceptable since contention here is between at most 3 workers over a short critical section, not a production reliability concern.

fitness.property: The lock acquisition path contains no custom while/for+sleep retry construct
fitness.verification: code-reviewer greps the three reagent-map-*.spec.ts files touched by this order for a hand-rolled retry loop around the lock file open; none should be present outside the expect(...).toPass(...) call

structuralDecisions.decision: Guard against a permanently stuck lock: before each acquisition attempt inside the toPass() callback, if fs.openSync throws EEXIST, stat the lock file and fs.unlinkSync it when its mtime is older than a named STALE_LOCK_MS constant (recommend 30_000, comfortably above the suite's per-test and REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS=5000 budgets) before retrying.
structuralDecisions.rationale: Without this, a worker process that crashes or is killed mid-test while holding the lock leaves every later run against the same machine's temp directory deadlocked indefinitely, with no automated recovery and no visible cause.
tradeOffs: A worker that is merely slow (not crashed) past STALE_LOCK_MS could have its lock forcibly stolen by another worker, in principle letting two test bodies touch expeditions.json concurrently for a brief window — accepted because 30s is far above any observed single-test duration in this suite, and the alternative (no staleness handling) is a hard hang, which is worse.

developerHandoffNotes: Add to apps/ye-olde-magic-shop/tests/reagent-map-api.spec.ts (exported for import elsewhere): a LOCK_PATH constant = path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'reagent-map-expeditions.lock'); a STALE_LOCK_MS constant = 30_000; acquireExpeditionsLock(): await expect(() => { try { fs.closeSync(fs.openSync(LOCK_PATH, 'wx')); } catch (err) { if ((err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'EEXIST' && Date.now() - fs.statSync(LOCK_PATH).mtimeMs > STALE_LOCK_MS) fs.unlinkSync(LOCK_PATH); throw err; } }).toPass({ timeout: 30_000 }); releaseExpeditionsLock(): fs.unlinkSync(LOCK_PATH).
